## Goal
Create a source-level dependency and responsibility audit for Tiny Swarm World's architecture boundaries before structural refactoring begins.

## Scope
Audit at minimum:
- `src/tiny_swarm_world/__main__.py`
- `src/tiny_swarm_world/installer.py`
- `src/tiny_swarm_world/simple_installer.py`
- `src/tiny_swarm_world/infrastructure/composition.py`
- root-level modules importing both application/domain and concrete infrastructure

Identify:
- forbidden dependency direction
- direct Docker/runtime access
- direct subprocess/filesystem/environment access
- runtime-specific branching
- raw config objects crossing boundaries
- duplicated lifecycle behavior
- circular dependencies
- cross-boundary debt

Classify each responsibility as `ENTRYPOINT`, `PRESENTATION`, `APPLICATION_ORCHESTRATION`, `COMPOSITION`, `INFRASTRUCTURE_ADAPTER`, `DOMAIN_POLICY`, `CROSS_BOUNDARY_DEBT`, or `LEGACY_COMPATIBILITY`.

## Deliverables
- dependency map
- architecture violation inventory
- responsibility ownership map
- remediation priority per finding
- baseline for later architecture fitness checks

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Relevant modules are inventoried.
- [ ] Every cross-boundary finding has an intended owner and migration path.
- [ ] Critical violations are ranked separately from maintainability debt.
- [ ] No refactor is proposed solely based on file size.
- [ ] Audit results are documented in the repository and referenced from #313.
title: [ARCH-03.01] Audit Layer Dependencies and Produce Architecture Violation Map

## Goal
Define formal dependency contracts between domain, application, ports, infrastructure, interfaces, and bootstrap/composition and enforce them automatically.

## Required Rules
- domain MUST NOT import infrastructure or interfaces
- application MUST NOT import concrete infrastructure adapters or CLI code
- infrastructure MAY depend on application/domain contracts
- interfaces MAY depend on application services
- bootstrap/composition MAY know concrete adapters
- root-level modules must not bypass these rules

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Architecture contracts are documented.
- [ ] Automated tests/import contracts enforce them.
- [ ] A deliberately introduced forbidden import fails CI.
- [ ] Existing justified exceptions are explicit and traceable.
- [ ] No new exception is added merely to keep the build green.

Implemented on published main `33aaafd5b80a3f316f4d650a9a831734dc7077e0`; reviewed as part of EPIC #313. No new product code was required for this status correction.

## Problem
The LXC node provider still combines resource qualification, provider selection, lifecycle execution and verification responsibilities in one central adapter. This increases maintenance risk and makes resource-qualification regressions harder to isolate.

## Goal
Extract LXC resource qualification into a focused infrastructure adapter/package with one explicit responsibility while preserving existing lifecycle, provider-selection and verification contracts.

## Scope
In scope:
- resource qualification and capability checks currently owned by `src/tiny_swarm_world/infrastructure/adapters/clients/lxc_node_provider.py`;
- explicit adapter boundary;
- tests for supported/unsupported resource states;
- delegation from the existing LXC provider;
- preservation of existing `PortNodeLifecycle`, `ProviderSelection` and `VerificationResult` contracts.

Out of scope:
- provider migration;
- changes to Incus lifecycle semantics;
- Kubernetes support;
- unrelated CLI refactoring;
- speculative generic runtime abstractions not required by current behavior.

## Architecture intent
This is a concrete hotspot-decomposition slice of EPIC #313. Resource qualification must become an independently testable infrastructure concern instead of remaining bundled with provider selection, lifecycle execution and verification.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The extracted adapter has one explicit responsibility and remains in infrastructure.
- [ ] The LXC provider delegates resource qualification to the extracted adapter.
- [ ] Lifecycle and verification behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] `PortNodeLifecycle`, `ProviderSelection` and `VerificationResult` contracts remain compatible.
- [ ] Supported and unsupported resource states have focused tests.
- [ ] Existing regression scenarios for node qualification, provider selection and lifecycle failure propagation pass.
- [ ] Architecture tests pass.
- [ ] Full local quality gate passes.
- [ ] Before/after maintenance evidence records affected modules and residual risk.
- [ ] No unnecessary abstraction is introduced beyond the actual qualification boundary.
title: [ARCH-03.23] Extract LXC Resource Qualification Adapter

Related: #347 (ARCH-03.04 — Extract Platform Preflight Use Case), #363 (ARCH-03.20 — Live/E2E compatibility validation)

## Problem
Preflight currently guarantees only the checks actually produced. Direct/custom construction can omit optional resource, filesystem, secret-storage and artifact-source collaborators, and malformed inspector results can omit checks. General summary writes swallow OSError/ValueError, while protected filesystem-override evidence failures already block correctly.

## Goal
Make collaborator completeness and evidence completeness explicit at the preflight architecture boundary without weakening standard setup, compatibility behavior, fail-closed safety controls, or RC1 evidence semantics.

## Scope
Define explicit collaborator completeness and summary-persistence contracts.

Cover:
- distinction between standard setup and intentionally partial/custom construction;
- missing collaborators;
- malformed inspector output;
- absent live filesystem authorizer;
- OSError/ValueError during summary persistence;
- preservation of existing failures;
- unexpected exception propagation;
- protected override authorizer fail-closed behavior;
- separation between executed-check success and evidence completeness;
- separation between local preflight success and release-evidence acceptance.

## Architecture intent
This issue hardens the boundary introduced/clarified by ARCH-03.04. Preflight must expose both operational qualification and evidence completeness explicitly rather than allowing missing collaborators or persistence failures to remain implicit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Standard setup is distinguishable from intentionally partial/custom construction.
- [ ] Missing collaborators are represented explicitly rather than silently interpreted as successful qualification.
- [ ] Malformed inspector output is detected and handled deterministically.
- [ ] Missing live filesystem authorizer behavior is covered.
- [ ] OSError/ValueError summary-write failures are covered explicitly.
- [ ] Existing expected failures remain preserved.
- [ ] Unexpected exceptions continue to propagate according to the established failure contract.
- [ ] Protected filesystem-override evidence failures remain fail-closed.
- [ ] Evidence completeness is reported separately from the result of executed checks.
- [ ] Local preflight success remains distinct from RC1/release-evidence acceptance.
- [ ] Architecture and regression tests cover the resulting contract.

## Existing evidence
Independent R09 review on `320f11f8722cb26fa289326178cae8a6486df1b5`: 57 existing preflight/authorizer tests passed on Python 3.12.14 and eight in-memory checks reproduced these boundaries. Missing collaborators are bounded maintenance debt for incomplete/custom wiring; general summary-write suppression also applies to standard wiring. Protected override evidence failures remain fail-closed.

This evidence does not imply that standard setup omits mandatory collaborators.

Refs: #310, #302.
title: [ARCH-03.22] Make Preflight Collaborator and Evidence Completeness Explicit
